cards.title: Introduction to Package Management
cards.content:
Package management in Python allows you to install, upgrade, configure, and remove third-party libraries and modules that are not part of the standard library.

The standard tool for this in the Python ecosystem is pip.

options.text: The standard package installer for Python

cards.title: Common pip Commands
cards.content:
Here are the most frequently used pip commands:

  • Install a package: pip install package_name
  • Uninstall a package: pip uninstall package_name
  • List installed packages: pip list
  • Save installed packages to a file: pip freeze > requirements.txt

cards.title: Why Virtual Environments?
cards.content:
Virtual environments allow you to manage separate package installations for different projects.

They solve the "it works on my machine" problem by preventing version conflicts between global Python packages and project-specific dependencies.

python -m venv myenv

steps: Create the virtual environment using python -m venv venv
Install project dependencies using pip install
Save dependencies to requirements.txt using pip freeze

cards.title: Modern Package Managers
cards.content:
While pip and venv are the traditional tools, modern Python development often utilizes higher-level dependency managers like Poetry or Pipenv.

These tools handle virtual environments, dependency resolution, and publishing packages in a single workflow using files like pyproject.toml.
